- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.10) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–10 days.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast decline, it often overcorrects; cap peak forecast at 10–15% below true peak.  
- If true outcome is consistently lower than forecast in first 5–7 days of horizon, apply downward bias of 3–8% to early days.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.10) and forecast is high, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 3–5 days.  
- If forecast mean is > 10% above true mean over 30d, apply mean reversion correction: subtract 1.5–3x the deviation from forecast mean.  
- For sentiment history with repeated +0.20 to +0.30 spikes, model tends to overreact; cap forecast at 10–15% below sentiment peak.  
- If forecast shows strong downward trend after spike, true outcome often rebounds; add 2–5% upward bias to next 3–7 days.
